definitions.explanation: Prefix attached to nouns, adjectives, and verb stems to show respect or politeness. Used with native Japanese words (和語).
Some words have become so common with お〜 that it's now considered a standard part of the word and isn't particularly honorific, just polite or refined.

examples.japanese: お{名前|なまえ}は{何|なん}ですか。
お{忙|いそが}しいところ、すみません。
examples.english: I'm sorry to bother you when you're busy.

examples.japanese: お{風呂|ふろ}に{入|はい}る。
お{菓子|かし}を{食|た}べる。
お{仕事|しごと}は{何|なん}ですか。

examples.english: Sorry to have kept you waiting.

notes:
USAGE RULES:
- お〜: Used with native Japanese words ({和語|わご})
- ご〜: Used with Sino-Japanese words ({漢語|かんご})

COMMON お〜 WORDS:
- お{水|みず} (water)
- お{茶|ちゃ} (tea)
- お{酒|さけ} (sake, alcohol)
- お{金|かね} (money)
- お{名前|なまえ} (name)
- お{仕事|しごと} (work, job)
- お{元気|げんき} (health, energy)

WORDS THAT ALWAYS USE お〜:
- お{腹|なか} (stomach) - rarely used without お
- お{箸|はし} (chopsticks) - standard
- お{風呂|ふろ} (bath) - standard
- お{菓子|かし} (sweets) - standard

HONORIFIC VERB PATTERNS:
- お + verb stem + になる (honorific action)
- お + verb stem + する (humble action)

Example: {先生|せんせい}がお{帰|かえ}りになった (The teacher went home - honorific).
